A boundary of converging winds from the west and northeast has lined 
up over Guam, resulting in scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms early this evening that could spread to Rota in the 
next few hours. A similar boundary will move over Saipan and Tinian 
around midnight, leading to scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms that will continue through Friday. Afterwards, a weak 
circulation embedded within the monsoon trough currently west of the 
region will invigorate showers and convection mainly over Guam and 
Rota into the weekend. Model guidance indicates this circulation 
quickly passing through the Marianas and heading north, so isolated 
shower coverage may return to the southern islands towards the end of
the weekend. As for Saipan and Tinian, drier air ahead of Tropical 
Storm Koguma (27W) may be enough to keep these islands in isolated 
shower coverage from Friday night on. Afterwards, benign weather
conditions are possible next week.

Marine...
Altimetry and surf observations have settled down from yesterday, so
combined seas of 5 to 7 ft tonight will drop to 4 to 6 ft Friday.
Light to gentle southwest to west winds will continue for Guam and
Rota, with light and variable winds for Saipan and Tinian for the
next few periods. A long-period northeasterly swell will reach the
region tonight in addition to the current southwesterly monsoon 
swell, but rip currents will remain a moderate risk along north, 
east, and west facing reefs.

Tropical Systems...
At 1 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Koguma was located near 
17N161E, moving northwest at 9 mph. Koguma is expected to move toward
the west-northwest over the next couple of days. Maximum sustained 
winds are at 65 mph. Koguma is expected to continue to slowly 
strengthen over the next few days, possibly becoming a typhoon later 
today. TS Koguma looks to remain over the open ocean, with no direct 
impacts to the Marianas or Micronesia. 

For more information on TS Koguma, see bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
No major changes to the forecast for Pohnpei and Kosrae. Still
looking at an overall dry pattern continuing through the weekend.
Showers look to increase early next week as the monsoon trough
reorients back to the south as it breaks away from TS Koguma. For
Majuro, a weak trough moving through the Marshalls, south of the
monsoon trough, is producing scattered showers across the atoll this
afternoon. These showers look to decrease through the night, likely 
becoming isolated by Friday morning, possibly earlier. Otherwise, a 
brief period of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms is 
possible Saturday night into Sunday as the monsoon trough reorients. 
This convection looks to move west of the Marshalls by Sunday 
afternoon. Otherwise, a dry pattern will continue into next week.

Benign marine conditions look to continue through the beginning of
next week, with mostly light to gentle winds and seas between 3 and 5
feet. Pohnpei and Kosrae will see occasional moderate winds through
Friday.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery late this afternoon shows an active regime over far
western Micronesia, with numerous to widespread locally heavy 
showers and isolated to scattered thunderstorms extending across much
of northern Yap State, including over Yap. Showers extend from west
to east within the moderate west to southwest monsoon flow across the
region, south of a weak circulation located west of the Marianas. A
series of outflow boundaries has been pushing southward into Yap
State from deep convection earlier in the day, converging with 
eastward-propagating outflow from just east of the Republic of 
Palau, which has been maintaining heavy thunderstorms near Yap this 
afternoon. Conditions are relatively dry over Palau for now, but
moist convergent monsoon flow will maintain scattered showers there
through at least Saturday. For Yap, numerous locally heavy showers
and isolated thunderstorms are expected to continue tonight, then
showers decrease slightly to scattered through Friday night, before
becoming numerous once more on Saturday, with model guidance
showing more robust convergence setting up over the area as winds
shift more southerly. Far to the east, Chuuk will remain mostly dry
through the next few days under the influence of broad, persistent 
ridging, which looks to break down around Tuesday as the monsoonal
westerlies strengthen and shift south into the area, which models
hint will be in potential response to a developing monsoon 
disturbance north of eastern Micronesia.

Benign marine conditions continue across the region, and look to
continue through the forecast period. Buoy and altimetry data
